text.p: AMR Corp's American Airlines unit said a new labor contract proposal put forward by its pilots was unacceptable because it would place excessive costs on the carrier.
"Their proposal would make our ability to manage the airline impossible," airline spokesman Al Comeaux told Reuters.

The Allied Pilots Association last week rejected a tentative four-year contract with the airline and has drawn up a list of fresh demands, including wage hikes, increased stock options and a guarantee that AMR's commuter carrier American Eagle would not be allowed to fly regional jets.
But airline management said the carrier had given up enough in striking a tentative agreement reached last September after two years of negotiations.
Comeaux said that original agreement, now rejected by pilots, had "pushed the limits of our ability to compete" and that the pilots' new proposal was unacceptable.

He said it would jeopardize the carrier's growth plans, including the order for at least 103 Boeing Co. jets which was announced two months ago but which was put on hold after pilots rejected the contract agreement on January 8.
